cases.name: method-off-no-fallback
cases.why: Nothing is the language's empty result: undefined, null, None or the zero value.

cases.name: method-on-with-fallback
cases.why: A supplied fallback must not be used while the toggle is on.

cases.name: async-method-off-no-fallback
cases.why: A null return here breaks an await at the call site, so the empty result must be an already-resolved promise.

cases.name: class-off-no-fallback
cases.why: The class is replaced by a shell that still constructs and still answers every method of the original, each returning nothing.

cases.name: class-evaluated-once-on-then-off
cases.why: The toggle is on at decoration and flipped off before use. A class is evaluated once, so the original stays in place -- this is what makes a reload behave identically in every port.

cases.name: class-evaluated-once-off-then-on
cases.why: The mirror image: off at decoration, on afterwards. The fallback stays, because the decision was already made.

cases.name: method-evaluated-every-call-on-then-off
cases.why: The opposite of the class rule: a method sees the flip and switches to the fallback on the next call.

cases.name: no-provider-method
cases.why: The error belongs at decoration time. Deferring it to the first call turns a startup misconfiguration into a runtime surprise in whichever code path happens to run first.
